text: Five minutes at Valencia. Three minutes against Feyenoord. Five at Levante. Eight against Racing. Four matches in a row, and Barcelona are on the scoreboard inside ten minutes every single time. That matters beyond the obvious advantage of being one goal up. An opponent can spend the entire week preparing to stay compact, protect the middle, and wait for one counterattack. Then the plan is chasing the game almost immediately. Stay deep, and Barcelona can keep working the ball around your box. Push more players forward, and suddenly there is space behind you. An early goal does not guarantee control. We will get to that. But it makes every decision more uncomfortable. And when your league record reads six wins, twenty-eight scored and six conceded, opponents cannot simply hope the first wave will be the last. The next question is where that first wave is coming from.
